context.analysis:
## Overview
[System: Hybrid Insurance Claims Modernization Platform. Purpose: Incrementally replaces a legacy mainframe with a modern Azure platform while maintaining data consistency.]

## Key Elements
- Customers and Brokers: External users submitting claims online.
- Claims Adjusters: Internal users managing claims via the modern web application.
- Modern Web Application: Azure App Service container hosting adjuster screens.
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL): Microservice container managing dynamic routing, feature flags, and contract mapping.
- Azure Service Bus: Message broker handling asynchronous communication.
- COBOL/DB2 Mainframe: On-premise system of record.

## Relationships
- Customers/Brokers to Modern Web Application via HTTPS (REST).
- Adjusters to Modern Web Application via HTTPS (REST, SSO via Active Directory).
- Modern Web Application to Azure Service Bus via AMQP/HTTPS.
- Anti-Corruption Layer to COBOL/DB2 Mainframe via MQ/TCP with Circuit Breakers.

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service: PaaS for hosting web apps to reduce cloud infrastructure overhead.
- Azure Service Bus: Managed message broker enabling asynchronous decoupling and DLQ error handling.
- OpenAPI/AsyncAPI: Frameworks for contract-first API design.
- Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC): Standardized deployment templates with guardrails.

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture uses an Anti-Corruption Layer and asynchronous messaging to decouple the modern Azure platform from rigid mainframe constraints. This ensures sub-2-second UI responses, strict data consistency, and rapid claim-type rollbacks despite the team's limited cloud experience.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a hybrid cloud-based Insurance Claims Modernization platform that gradually replaces a legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe. Its core purpose is to enable online submissions and streamlined adjuster workflows while ensuring continuous synchronization with the legacy system of record.]

## Key Elements
- Customers and Brokers (Users)
- Claims Adjusters (Users)
- COBOL/DB2 Mainframe (External System of Record)
- API Gateway Container
- Customer BFF Container and Adjuster BFF Container
- Modular Monolith Container (Azure)
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) Container
- Routing / Feature Flag Container
- Data Sync / Reconciliation Container
- Asynchronous Messaging & Caching Layer (Azure Service Bus and Redis)
- IAM Proxy / Token Exchange Container
- Observability & Logging Container (Azure Application Insights)
- Configuration & Secrets Management Container (Azure Key Vault)

## Relationships
- Customers/Brokers interact with Customer BFF via HTTPS (TLS 1.3)
- Claims Adjusters interact with Adjuster BFF via HTTPS (TLS 1.3)
- BFFs communicate with API Gateway via internal HTTPS/REST
- API Gateway routes traffic through Routing/Feature Flag Container to Modular Monolith via internal REST/gRPC
- Modular Monolith communicates with COBOL/DB2 Mainframe via Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) over secure VPN/TLS
- Modular Monolith utilizes Azure Service Bus (AMQP) for async processing and Redis for caching
- IAM Proxy integrates with insurer's Active Directory via SAML/OAuth2/OIDC
- Observability layer collects telemetry from all Azure containers

## Technology Stack
- Azure West Europe: Primary cloud region for new platform components
- Azure App Service / Container Apps: Hosting environment for modular monolith and BFFs
- Azure Service Bus & Redis: Asynchronous messaging and caching to mitigate 5s mainframe latency
- Azure Application Insights: Centralized observability, distributed tracing, and synthetic monitoring
- Azure Key Vault: Centralized configuration and secrets management
- Azure DevOps / GitHub Actions: CI/CD automation and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC)

## Rationale
[A hybrid Strangler Fig pattern with a modular monolith minimizes risk for a team with limited cloud experience while isolating complex legacy dependencies. Asynchronous caching and BFFs guarantee sub-2-second UI performance, and the ACL ensures strict 1-day rollbacks.]

API Gateway Container.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a hybrid insurance claims modernization platform that gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a modern Azure-based cloud architecture. Its core purpose is to enable online claim submissions and adjuster workflows while maintaining zero data loss and strict performance standards.]

## Key Elements
- API Gateway Container (Azure API Management / Azure Container Apps)
- Customer BFF Container (Azure App Service / Container Apps)
- Adjuster BFF Container (Azure App Service / Container Apps)
- Modular Monolith Container (Azure App Service / Container Apps)
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) Container (Azure Container Apps)
- Routing / Feature Flag Container (Container Apps)
- Asynchronous Messaging & Caching Layer (Azure Service Bus and Redis)
- COBOL/DB2 Mainframe (On-premises system of record)

## Relationships
- Customer BFF Container -> API Gateway Container: Communicates via internal APIs [Internal HTTPS/REST]
- Adjuster BFF Container -> API Gateway Container: Communicates via internal APIs [Internal HTTPS/REST]
- API Gateway Container -> Routing / Feature Flag Container: Evaluates rules [In-memory SDK with local Redis cache]
- API Gateway Container -> Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) Container: Routes legacy traffic [HTTPS/REST]

## Technology Stack
- Azure API Management: Edge security, rate limiting, and declarative resilience policies
- Redis: Caching feature flags, idempotency keys, and edge response caching
- Azure Container Apps / App Service: Hosting modern microservices and BFFs
- RFC 7807 (Problem Details): Standardized error formatting
- OpenTelemetry / Azure Application Insights: Hybrid end-to-end tracing via correlation IDs

## Rationale
[The hybrid architecture utilizes an API Gateway with local caching and strict resilience policies to protect against mainframe latency and ensure sub-2-second adjuster screens. Centralized edge security, versioning, and an Anti-Corruption Layer enable iterative claim migration and rapid one-day rollbacks.]

Customer BFF Container.analysis:
## Overview
- Hybrid insurance claims modernization platform replacing a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe.
- Enables online claim submissions and adjuster web applications while maintaining legacy continuity.

## Key Elements
- Customers and Brokers (External users)
- Customer BFF Container (Azure App Service / Container Apps)
- API Gateway Container (Azure Container Apps / API Management)
- Routing / Feature Flag Container (Container Apps)
- Modular Monolith Container (Azure App Service / Container Apps)
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) Container (Azure Container Apps)
- Observability & Logging Container (Azure Application Insights)
- Configuration & Secrets Management Container (Azure Key Vault)

## Relationships
- Customers and Brokers -> Customer BFF Container: Online claim submission [HTTPS (TLS 1.3)]
- Customer BFF Container -> API Gateway Container: Internal API routing [Internal HTTPS/REST]
- Customer BFF Container -> Routing / Feature Flag Container: Dynamic routing checks [Internal REST]
- Customer BFF Container -> Configuration & Secrets Management Container: Secret retrieval [Azure SDK / HTTPS]
- Observability & Logging Container -> Customer BFF Container: Telemetry collection [Telemetry SDK]

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service / Container Apps: Provides scalable, stateless hosting suitable for limited cloud experience.
- Azure Key Vault: Externalizes configuration and secrets for secure management.
- Azure Application Insights: Centralizes telemetry with strict PII scrubbing and correlation IDs.
- OpenAPI/Swagger: Standardizes API contracts between the BFF and API Gateway.

## Rationale
- The architecture isolates complex cloud dependencies in the BFF while enabling rapid feature flag rollbacks to the mainframe.
- Stateless scaling, circuit breakers, and presigned URLs ensure high availability and performance despite legacy latency.

Adjuster BFF Container.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a hybrid Insurance Claims Modernization platform that gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a cloud-native Azure architecture. Its core purpose is to enable seamless online claims submission and adjuster workflows while maintaining zero downtime and strict data consistency.]

## Key Elements
- Adjuster BFF Container (Azure App Service / Container Apps)
- API Gateway Container (Azure Container Apps / API Management)
- Asynchronous Messaging & Caching Layer (Azure Service Bus and Redis)
- Routing / Feature Flag Container (Container Apps)
- Observability & Logging Container (Azure Application Insights)
- Configuration & Secrets Management Container (Azure Key Vault)
- COBOL/DB2 Mainframe (On-premises system of record)

## Relationships
- Claims Adjusters -> Adjuster BFF Container: Interacts for adjuster workflows via HTTPS (TLS 1.3)
- Adjuster BFF Container -> API Gateway Container: Communicates via internal APIs using Internal HTTPS/REST
- Observability & Logging Container -> Adjuster BFF Container: Collects telemetry via Telemetry SDK

## Technology Stack
- Azure Container Apps: Chosen for hosting containers with managed ingress and scaling, matching the team's need for simplicity despite limited cloud experience.
- Redis Cache: Selected for offloading session state and pre-fetching read-models to guarantee sub-2s screen loads (R-05).
- OpenAPI & Schema Validation Middleware: Utilized for contract-first development and early payload validation to protect downstream legacy systems.
- Azure Key Vault: Implemented for centralized, secure configuration and secrets management via environment injection.
- W3C Trace Context & Structured JSON Logging: Adopted for distributed tracing and rapid incident triage across the hybrid network boundary.

## Rationale
[This architecture decouples modern user interfaces from a brittle mainframe using a stateless Backend-For-Frontend and caching layer, satisfying strict performance and rollback requirements (R-05, R-06). Furthermore, it simplifies operational complexity for a cloud-inexperienced team by leveraging managed Azure services while preserving business continuity.]

Modular Monolith Container.analysis:
## Overview
[The hybrid system gradually replaces a legacy 30-year-old mainframe claims platform with a modern cloud-native modular monolith while maintaining continuous operations. It enables online claims submission and adjuster management while ensuring zero data loss and seamless legacy fallback.]

## Key Elements
- Customers and Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- COBOL/DB2 Mainframe (System of Record)
- API Gateway Container (Azure Container Apps / API Management)
- Customer BFF Container (Azure App Service / Container Apps)
- Adjuster BFF Container (Azure App Service / Container Apps)
- Modular Monolith Container (Azure App Service / Container Apps)
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) Container (Azure Container Apps)
- Routing / Feature Flag Container (Container Apps)
- Data Sync / Reconciliation Container (Azure Container Apps)
- Asynchronous Messaging & Caching Layer (Azure Service Bus and Redis)
- IAM Proxy / Token Exchange Container (Container Apps)
- Observability & Logging Container (Azure Application Insights)
- Configuration & Secrets Management Container (Azure Key Vault)

## Relationships
- Customers and Brokers -> API Gateway Container: Submits claims [HTTPS/REST]
- Claims Adjusters -> API Gateway Container: Manages claims [HTTPS/REST]
- API Gateway Container -> Customer BFF Container: Routes customer traffic [HTTP/REST]
- API Gateway Container -> Adjuster BFF Container: Routes adjuster traffic [HTTP/REST]
- Routing / Feature Flag Container -> Modular Monolith Container: Forwards routed traffic [Internal REST/gRPC]
- Modular Monolith Container -> Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) Container: Communicates with legacy system [Internal REST/gRPC]
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) Container -> COBOL/DB2 Mainframe: Synchronizes legacy claims [SNA / IBM MQ / Batch]
- Modular Monolith Container -> Asynchronous Messaging & Caching Layer: Utilizes for async processing and caching [AMQP and Redis Protocol]
- Observability & Logging Container -> Modular Monolith Container: Collects telemetry [Telemetry SDK]

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service / Container Apps: Hosts modern micro-containers with low initial cloud operational overhead.
- Azure Service Bus & Redis: Provides reliable async messaging and low-latency read caching to bypass mainframe latency.
- Hexagonal / Clean Architecture: Isolates domain logic from infrastructure to facilitate future service extraction.
- NetArchTest / ArchUnit: Enforces strict internal module boundaries and dependency rules automatically via CI/CD.
- Azure App Configuration & Key Vault: Manages centralized feature flags and secrets to support one-day rollbacks.

## Rationale
[A modular monolith architecture reduces distributed systems complexity for a team with limited cloud experience while maintaining strict internal boundaries for future extraction. Hybrid integration patterns, outbox/inbox mechanisms, and feature flags guarantee regulatory consistency, sub-2-second UI responses, and rapid legacy rollback capabilities.]

## Overview
[The Routing / Feature Flag Container manages dynamic request routing and feature flag evaluations to support the gradual migration of insurance claim types. It ensures high-performance, resilient traffic splitting between the legacy mainframe and the modern platform.]

- Routing / Feature Flag Container -> Observability Container: Emits asynchronous audit logs and telemetry via OpenTelemetry

- OpenFeature standard: Adopts an open specification for feature flag and routing evaluations to avoid proprietary lock-in

- Azure Application Insights: Collects structured telemetry, evaluation latency metrics, and audit logs

[Separating routing and feature flag logic into a dedicated container decouples migration switching from core application code, ensuring rapid one-day rollbacks. Caching evaluations and implementing strict timeouts protect system performance and meet the sub-2-second adjuster screen requirement despite limited team cloud experience.]

Asynchronous Messaging & Caching Layer.analysis:
## Overview
This system modernizes a regional insurer's 30-year-old mainframe by incrementally migrating claim types to a hybrid Azure cloud platform. It ensures zero data loss and seamless coexistence with the legacy COBOL/DB2 system of record.

## Key Elements
- **Azure Service Bus**: Handles asynchronous messaging, event publishing, and dead-letter queues.
- **Azure Cache for Redis**: Provides high-performance caching for read-heavy reference data.
- **Azure Blob Storage**: Stores large binary files via the Claim Check pattern.
- **Modular Monolith**: Core business logic container processing claims and consuming messages.
- **Azure Application Insights**: Collects telemetry, metrics, and distributed tracing.

## Relationships
- **Modular Monolith -> Azure Service Bus**: Publishes and consumes domain events using AMQP with W3C trace context headers.
- **Modular Monolith -> Azure Cache for Redis**: Reads and writes cached reference data using the Redis Protocol via Cache-Aside pattern.
- **Modular Monolith -> Azure Blob Storage**: Offloads and retrieves large binary documents using HTTPS.
- **Azure Service Bus -> Azure Application Insights**: Emits telemetry for dead-letter queues and message processing states.

## Technology Stack
- **Azure Service Bus**: Chosen for reliable managed queuing, dead-letter support, and at-least-once delivery guarantees.
- **Azure Cache for Redis**: Selected for low-latency read caching to shield the legacy mainframe from performance bottlenecks.
- **Transactional Outbox Pattern**: Implemented in the database to eliminate dual-write failures during event publishing.
- **Claim Check Pattern**: Used with Azure Blob Storage to keep message payload sizes small and maintain throughput.

## Rationale
This architecture uses managed Azure cloud components to simplify operations for a team with limited cloud experience while guaranteeing zero message loss. It isolates the expensive-to-change mainframe through robust asynchronous messaging and caching patterns.

## Overview
The system is a hybrid Insurance Claims Modernization platform that gradually replaces a 30-year-old mainframe with a cloud-native architecture. Its core purpose is to enable online claims submission and adjuster web applications while maintaining operational continuity with the on-premise COBOL/DB2 system.

## Key Elements

- Active Directory (On-premise / Enterprise IDP)

- API Gateway Container -> IAM Proxy / Token Exchange Container: Validates incoming requests and inspects JWT claims

- Azure App Service Authentication (Easy Auth) / RFC 8693: Standardizes token exchange without custom protocol translation to reduce security risks
- Azure Key Vault: Dynamically supplies immutable configuration, issuer mappings, and secrets at startup to prevent configuration drift
- Redis: Caches tokens to accelerate validation checks and protect sub-2-second adjuster screen load performance
- W3C Trace Context: Propagates correlation IDs across the hybrid boundary for end-to-end observability in Application Insights

## Rationale
This architecture balances strict legacy constraints with cloud modernization by isolating authentication logic in a managed, scalable proxy. It protects an inexperienced cloud team through standard protocols and automated health checks while ensuring data consistency and sub-2-second performance across the hybrid boundary.
